what_worked: Power-law concentration framing and top-company bar chart communicate skewness clearly.
fix_next: The category revenue chart uses all-time data but contradicts the frozen 30-day reference dataset; verify every number against the actual dataset columns.
verdict: Thin, inaccurate five-slide deck that describes charts without genuine analysis.
factual_error_detail: Slide 4: Chart shows E-commerce as highest all-time category (~$54M) above AI; reference shows AI is highest ($2.36M 30-day) and E-comm is third—ranking is wrong regardless of time window. Slide 4: Stripe stated as 64% of companies; reference is 636/1000=63.6%, minor but the denominator context (by revenue share $13.5M/$15.6M=86.7%) is omitted. Slide 2: 30-day revenue $15.6M is correct, but '61% top 1% share' is unverifiable and likely refers to all-time, not 30-day; top-10 (1%) 30-day share is 49.6% per reference, not 61%. Slide 5: Correlation r=0.92 between 30-day and all-time revenue is presented without methodology; the only frozen correlation (founded-year vs revenue) is r=0.025, and no 30-day/all-time r is provided in reference—claim is unverifiable and likely inflated by outliers without log-transform disclosure. Slide 4: No acknowledgment of 274 missing category values, making category totals misleading.

evidence.insight: Slides mostly restate big numbers (total revenue, top companies) without actionable interpretation. The 'predictive correlation' on slide 5 is the only analytical claim but is unverified and lacks nuance about outlier-driven correlations.
evidence.narrative: Five slides move from overview → top companies → sectors → correlations, but there is no stated thesis, no synthesis slide, and no recommendations. The deck reads as a disconnected fact list.
evidence.framing: No audience is identified, no research question is posed, no limitations or missingness are disclosed. A cold reader cannot tell what decision this analysis serves. Scope mixes 30-day and all-time without clarifying which is primary.
evidence.accuracy: Category ranking on slide 4 contradicts reference data. Top-1% share of 61% doesn't match the 49.6% top-10 30-day figure. Correlation claims on slide 5 are unverifiable. Missing data (274 category, 241 country, 216 zero-revenue) never acknowledged.
evidence.visual: Clean, consistent template with good hierarchy and readable fonts. Bar charts are appropriately chosen. However, charts lack axis labels/units on some slides, and the category chart appears fabricated given data mismatch. Only two chart types across five slides.
evidence.ai_slop: Consulting-style language ('power-law reality,' 'high-confidence indicator,' 'dominant payment rail') without substantive backing. Template uniformity and inflated certainty suggest AI-generated content with minimal verification.
